analysis.title: "We Understand The Optics": Goldman Hikes Data Center Spending Forecasts Days After Voters "Froze" The Buildout
key_insights: Goldman's E&C analyst Adam Bubes raised US data center construction spending forecasts to $80B in 2026 and $100B in 2027 (from $67B and $87B) and introduced a $125B forecast for 2028, days after midterm elections put governors favoring build pauses in office in states with roughly 45% of planned US capacity.
US data center construction spending growth accelerated from 55% YoY in June to 90% YoY in September, with Q3 starts up meaningfully. The Census Bureau series runs at a SAAR of nearly $100B.

About 86GW is under construction, which Goldman prices at ~$3.5B per GW of construction cost (excluding servers, racks, GPUs, networking) for roughly $300B of total construction spend, about 6x 2025 US data center construction spending. Adding high-probability announcements expands the pipeline to ~$900B. Adding ~293GW of medium and low probability projects takes it to ~$1.9T, which Goldman calls a measure of pipeline value and not an estimate of spend.
Goldman estimates more than $200B of the under-construction pipeline has yet to be deployed. Projects already under construction are the ones a moratorium is least likely to touch.

Goldman IT hardware analyst Michael Ng: the US has 57GW-gross of active data center capacity, with 9GW-gross under construction taking it to 65GW by end-2026. Aterio tracks 78GW-gross under construction adding a net 33/37/8/0GW-gross in 2027/28/29/30. Counting only projects already being built, US capacity reaches 143GW by 2030.

At a 1.5 PUE, under-construction projects imply 22/24/5 GW-IT of net additions in 2027/28/29, against Goldman's forecasts of 20/24/23 GW-IT. Ng says this gives confidence in the recently revised forecasts, which he believes are conservative and likely below consensus.
Aterio counts another 137GW-gross of high-likelihood capacity (permitting, financing and power secured) slated for 2027-30.

Caveat from Ng: Aterio's definition of 'under construction' includes site work such as land clearing, grading and utility trenching, often done before a tenant is signed. A moratorium could still catch projects that lack an electricity services agreement or air permit.

The five states with hostile campaigns (Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia, Michigan) account for about 42% of under-construction and high-likelihood capacity. Texas alone is 26% of cumulative 2026-30 net additions, and 20% of 2027 and 27% of 2028 net additions counting only under-construction projects. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for an immediate moratorium.

Ng: moratoriums are not bans or cancellations. The risks to operators are ready-for-service delays (in some cases leading to contract cancellations), higher financing costs from longer construction, higher taxes from reduced tax breaks, and higher infrastructure capex.

Bubes: current timelines imply ~55GW energizing in 2028 alone, well above the historical pace, so Goldman already expected slippage to the right. Midterms add timing risk but he sees no change in underlying demand, and a possible outcome is smoothing spending and extending the cycle's duration without changing the TAM.

Goldman economists expect state pauses to be conditional and short-lived, in part because data centers ranked low among voter priorities. Federal legislation would need bipartisan Senate support and to overcome a veto.

For Goldman's construction coverage (FIX, EME, LGN), bookings typically follow project starts by about six months, which gives a timing buffer. Wells Fargo's Jerry Revich expects the Texas pause to last roughly through the legislative session (Jan 12 to May 31, 2027). The next datapoint is the Texas data center audit due December 10.

Stock exposure per Ng: IREN has the highest Texas exposure in his coverage (73%/87% of data center capacity in the state). Celestica (CLS) and Arista (ANET) would feel delays through servers and data center switches. Digital Realty (DLR) and Equinix (EQIX) have minimal exposure to development-heavy markets.

Goldman's forecast includes no speculative or medium probability announcements, only under-construction projects plus a conservative slice of high-probability ones. Under-construction projects alone carry double-digit spending growth through 2027 (to ~$105B). Including all high-probability announcements gives ~$155B in 2027 and a peak of ~$185B in 2028, with 2030 above 2026 levels.

Goldman would gain confidence in 2029-30 growth from continued new project announcements (projects pending construction are up 55% YoY), medium and low probability capacity graduating to high probability and breaking ground, or 2027-28 timelines slipping without cancellations.

Demand side: hyperscaler capex is on track for about $800B in 2026 and ~$1.3T in 2027 (FactSet consensus), and the three largest public cloud providers hold a combined revenue backlog above $1.7T. Wells Fargo cites H100 rental rates up 26% YoY and GB200 rental pricing up 50% YTD (12% in the past month).
Revich notes Texas Governor Abbott's September directive already caught projects with on-site generation, so the Texas freeze does not currently spare self-powered campuses.

Market context cited by the author: Nasdaq suffered its worst day since Covid (about 6% crash), tech hedge funds round-tripped their 2026 gains, Thursday was the biggest put day in Cboe history, data center CDS hit records, and Microsoft pulled an Oracle AI rental. The author sides with the optimists on construction but warns that delays hit levered developers (e.g. one paying 12.5% on a bond due 2028) hardest, so the debt is the fault line.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees 86GW already under construction and a ~$900B high-confidence pipeline. Moratoriums shift activity right without reducing the TAM, and hyperscaler capex of ~$800B in 2026 and ~$1.3T in 2027 plus a $1.7T cloud backlog support demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Moratoriums can delay ready-for-service dates, raise financing costs, remove tax breaks and cancel some contracts. Some 'under construction' projects are only site work and could be caught, and levered developers with expensive debt face existential risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of project cancellations (not only slippage), the Texas data center audit due December 10, or a Texas pause lasting beyond the legislative session ending May 31, 2027.
